newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ease as Tokyo stocks rise.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs ease as Tokyo stocks rise.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese Government Bond (JGB) futures lost more ground on Monday as Tokyo stocks headed higher and bearish sentiment persisted in the interest rate futures market.
Dealers said there was little in the way of fresh news but a weak technical outlook combined with uncertainty over the direction of Japan's rates weighed on the market.

"December Euroyen failed to clear resistance at 98.86. The market is basically expecting the Bank of Japan to hike rates by 50 basis points by year end. So people will sell on any rallies," a trader with a U.S. futures house said.
He said immediate support for the contract was at 98.75. It stood at 98.82 at 1110 GMT after falling to a low of 98.80 against its IMM close at 98.86.
A bank dealer said December Euroyen would trade in a broader range of 98.70-99.00 but could climb above that level after the June contract's expiry in two weeks.
"There could be some adjustment of the yield curve after the front contract's expiry," he said.
June JGBs ended at 123.91 against their opening 124.15, with players seen increasingly rolling over their positions to September, ahead of June's expiry on Friday.

Eurodollar futures ended slightly higher in thin trade following a strong close in Chicago last week, where improving technical factors and hopes the U.S. economy would continue to moderate in the second quarter lifted the market.
December Eurodollars ended at 93.790 against an IMM close at 93.770 on volume of 6,610 lots.
